rows: Severe thunderstorm winds damaged a barn and destroyed a shed.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down power lines in Marble Falls. Power was out to much of the town for about 4 hours.
A small tornado was spotted by the Burnet County Sheriff's Department as it touched down briefly in an open field near Lake Victor. No damage was noted.
The Burnet County Sheriff's Department reported that a second tornado touched down briefly near Oatmeal. It did not cause any visible damage.
A third small and short-lived tornado was spotted by a Burnet County Sheriff's Deputy as it crossed SH183 southeast of Briggs.

Severe thunderstorms struck the area between Marble Falls and Spicewood, knocking over trees, phone lines, and power lines. The winds, estimated near 65 knots, also damaged roofs in both Marble Falls and in Spicewood.

Severe thunderstorms uprooted trees and damaged roofs in the Granite Shoals area.
A roof was blown off a house.

Multiple trees were reported down or snapped across the county. A large bow echo moved through the county and produced wind damage mainly through the central sections of the county from Granite Shoals, to Marble Falls, to Burnet, and over to Bertram.

Storm survey revealed a small tornado crossed a wooded area and partially struck a mobile home on Overlook Trail. There was light damage to a parked vehicle in front of the home. A small porch was damaged and lumber was thrown into the front window. A large two by four was found …
Tree limbs reported down on 1431 just west of Marble Falls.
Law enforcement reported a brief tornado touchdown which uprooted a few trees at 3707 CR 101.
Marble Falls Police reported power lines and tree limbs down.
A resident reported a measured wind gust of 67 mph along with small hail and said some of their animals were missing as a result.

A thunderstorm moved across the Horseshoe Bay area and produced hail ranging from golf ball to hen egg size.
A thunderstorm moved from Marble Falls to Spicewood and produced hail ranging from half dollar to golf ball size.
A resident reported nickel to quarter size hail near Deer Creek Road northeast of Tow.

A peak wind of 58 kts was measured by the Burnet Airport ASOS. A NWS storm damage survey found several planes broken loose from their ties at the airport and either flipped over or skidded along the tarmac several hundred yards. Across the street from the airport one camper trail…

Widespread damage occurred in the town of Bertram as a large thunderstorm moved east through the town. Numerous large mature trees were uprooted in town as well as several buildings sustained roof damage. The damage survey estimates winds of 70 to 80 mph hit the town.
Large tree limbs were reported down in RV Park.

A thunderstorm produced a measured five inch diameter hailstone which ties the record for the largest hailstone ever reported in South Central Texas.
